correctness.rationale: For N>=5, direct spin-flip cancellation yields 2J times the five-word inequality. Every cyclic spin word maps bijectively to an N-step closed walk in the 16-state de Bruijn transfer graph, hence exact traces. All five allowed-word pattern regions are determined by the 32 possible local spin patterns, with neutral flips excluded at both ratios 2/3 and 2. Six characteristic polynomials are recomputed exactly by symbolic determinant, 42 trace counts agree with independently enumerated full Hamiltonian flips (six couplings, N=5..11), and maximal strongly connected recurrent components with self-loops prove primitive Perron asymptotics. Strict matrix inclusion across r=2 proves isolated entropy depression; limitations exclude quench kinetics and temperature effects.

value.rationale: Competition between ordinary ferromagnetic bonds and consecutive three-body Ising interactions is a natural physical interpolation between two established models, and determines zero-temperature metastable-state complexity. An isolated drop of exponential blocked-state entropy precisely at a neutral-flip threshold, lower than both adjacent coupling regimes, is a structural boundary effect—not a single small finite count or routine parameter retabulation. Exact thresholds, transfer polynomials and Perron growth rates supply benchmarks for studies of kinetic freezing and clarify the discontinuity produced by neutral-flip conventions. No dynamical trapping probabilities or thermodynamic phase transitions are asserted.
